newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares down in bourse on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: German shares down in bourse on profit taking.

text.p: The DAX index of 30 German blue-chips fell 1.5 percent in early bourse trade on Thursday in what dealers said was extremely volatile trade, but traders shrugged off talk of a crash.
"It's just extremely volatile at the moment. Nobody cares about a one percent movement either way anymore, we reckon there are just a few people taking profits out there," a broker said.
The DAX index pared losses as bourse continued to stand at 4,357.44 points, down 48.65 or 1.10 percent.
Earlier, its IBIS DAX electronic counterpart hit a new all-time high of 4,449.33.
Support for the market came from the ever-firmer dollar and a higher, if unspectacularly so, close on Wall Street.

"This market is like a train moving full-steam ahead, which means it is going to take a while for it to slow down. We could lose of couple of hundred points and it would not make any difference," a Frankfurt trader said.
As to whether or not the market is getting ready for a crash, dealers said that there was too much caution around.

"The word "crash" is on everyone's lips and people are saying the market is overheating. But look at the backdrop to this bull run -- low interest rates, weak mark -- and it's hard to see any evidence pointing to a real crash," he said.
Among individual sectors, focus was again on the banking sector which has chalked up monster gains in recent days.
Commerzbank AG and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG were centre of attention after both banks reported their first half 1997 figures early on.
Commerzbank said that its operating profit after provisions was up 23.2 percent at 1.63 billion marks, which was above analysts' expectations.

Bayerische Vereinsbank, which said earlier this week that it plans to merge with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank, saw its operating profit after provisions rise 15.2 percent to 765.7 million marks, somewhat below expectations.
Both shares had a rollercoaster ride in morning trade, but were particularly badly hit by profit-taking in bourse trade.
Commerzbank was down 2.70 marks at 62.30 marks, while Vereinsbank fell 13 percent early on, before paring losses to stand at 62.20 marks, down 2.80 marks.
Dealers were also closely monitoring retailer Metro AG, which split its shares on Wednesday, leading to some confusion and incorrect pricing.
Just before the end of electronic trade on Wednesday the bourse suspended trade in Metro and corrected the error in pricing.
Metro shares were up 1.17 marks at 92 marks pre-bourse.
